title: Can great games be made without subscription plan? Free Claude, Free Codex?
author: ChronoTriggered-
selftext:
Or you 100% need a subscription plan to these AI to get somewhere? 

I want to make a 2d rpg with Claude, Godot, Codex, Pixellab and wonder if going the free route is a bad idea from the get go.

comments.author: IndianaNetworkAdmin
comments.body:
If you have zero coding experience, there are still options out there. RPG Maker, if you like older style SNES-era JRPGs. They go up on Humble Bundle most years for dirt cheap along with basic assets. They've been around for ages, meaning you can easily get ChatGPT and other models to assist you with the complicated systems without having to dive fully into Fable 5.2 or anything costly.

Alternatively, if you want to code, I recommend Godot. There are MCPs out there like gdaimcp, but honestly GDScript is derived from a version of Python 3.x and just about any LLM can work with the files directly and use a headless mode for testing.  
  
There's an excellent game on Steam that's fairly cheap, The Farmer Was Replaced, that's gamified basic Python coding. If you have ADHD or another issue that makes normal learning difficult, gamified options like that are the way to go.
